newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government sees Thomson deal before spring.
newsitem.headline: French government sees Thomson deal before spring.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday he hoped the privatisation of Thomson SA would take place before the spring and did not rule out breaking up the company in the sale.
"It must be done as quickly as possible," Arthuis said in a radio interview. "I hope it will be done before the spring."
Arthuis said the government still wanted to sell Thomson in one piece but was not excluding the possibility of selling individual units.
"The overall plan is a sale in one piece but we must examine all the the hypotheses," he said when asked if a sale of individual units was possible. "We must not exclude anything."
France on Wednesday called off the sale of the state electronics group to Lagardere Groupe but President Jacques Chirac vowed to bring the sell-off to fruition.

The government, which had doggedly defended its choice amid a storm of employee protest and political opposition, made the U-turn after the Privatisation Commission challenged the terms of South Korean Daewoo's involvement in the sale.
Arthuis said on Wednesday that the chief difficulty in the privatisation process was the sale of Thomson's heavily-indebted Thomson Multimedia unit.
"The difficulty of finding a buyer for Thomson Multimedia...must not be underestimated," he said.

Arthuis defended the terms of the Thomson sale, planned as a private placement, saying the poor financial condition of Thomson and the strategic importance of Thomson's defence involvement made that process inevitable.

"The private placement was necessary for two reasons," Arthuis said. "First because it's the defence industry and the government necessarily has its word to say and then because it's a company in which unfortunately debts outweigh assets."

"The company has the strength of its men, its teams, its savoir faire, of an experience and of its markets no doubt, but unfortunately the situation on the financial front is such that a recapitalisation is needed, which makes a private placement necessary," Arthuis said.
Arthuis said the government had been in favour of the sale of Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo because it promised to create jobs and rescue the company from its financial distress.
"The government rallied to this idea because Daewoo was in a position to create jobs and dig Thomson out of its ditch," Arthuis said.
He added that it was the question of job creation that would require guarantees from Daewoo.
Daewoo has repeatedly promised to create as many as 5,000 jobs and invest more than $1.0 billion in France after taking over Thomson Multimedia.
